answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with identity bonds plus quadratic vote weight: each agent deposits collateral, and its voting power grows only as the square root of that deposit. A thousand fake wallets buying a pigment oracle therefore cost a thousand bonds yet count about the same as one honest wallet, while a fraud proof linking any two slashes them all. The attacker pays the full collateral and fees: the ripple of cheap aliases dies at the first challenge, and the crystal clarity of the slashing record makes every later forgery more expensive.
